rules.title: An attribute is a shape literal on a declaration, and nothing is ever declared or instantiated for it
rules.divergesFromPhp: an attribute is never an object — PHP builds a real one the first time `ReflectionAttribute::newInstance()` is called, and needs a declared `#[Attribute]` class for every attribute kind

rules.title: An attribute attaches at four declaration sites, and a named one's name is a shape-typed `type` alias
rules.divergesFromPhp: a named attribute resolves to a `type` alias rather than to a class, so there is no per-attribute-kind declaration and no second namespace of attribute names

rules.title: Every field value in an attribute payload is a compile-time constant
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP admits any expression as an attribute argument, `new` included, so building one has an execution order and side effects

rules.title: An attribute may be attached to one declaration any number of times, and attach time never counts them
rules.divergesFromPhp: repeatability is the default and needs no `Attribute::IS_REPEATABLE` marker

rules.title: A retrieval matches a payload by the shape it satisfies, never by the name it was attached under
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `ReflectionAttribute` and no lookup by attribute class name; two unrelated libraries can ask for the same shape without agreeing on a name

rules.title: A retrieval is answered while checking and replaced by its answer, so ambiguity is a compile error
rules.divergesFromPhp: "which one did I get?" for a repeated attribute is a diagnostic at the call site rather than a question a test run answers, and no reflection table reaches the compiled unit

rules.title: An explicit `<T>` at a call site is written for compiler-owned members only
rules.divergesFromPhp: `Foo::BAR < X > ($y)` reads as a call carrying a type argument where PHP reads two comparisons

rules.title: `#[Api]` may add to the generated document and may not contradict the code
rules.divergesFromPhp: an annotation that disagrees with the handler is a compile error rather than a documentation bug nobody notices

rules.title: A method carrying `#[Route]` carries `#[Access]`, and an omission does not compile
rules.divergesFromPhp: no PHP framework can refuse to build a route whose author wrote no access decision

rules.title: `#[Access]` names one resolvable decision in `allow`, and one of them covers a method
